answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because falcon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, cipher is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any zephyr approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
